## [2026-05-19] v1.1.0 Phase 6 -- Memory lifecycle CLI + Ebbinghaus decay + `/recall` `/remember` `/forget` slash commands

### Goal

Surface user-facing memory commands and run the decay sweep on idle. The plan ([docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/plans/phase-06-memory-cli-decay-and-slash-commands.md](v1/v1.1/plans/phase-06-memory-cli-decay-and-slash-commands.md)) adopts four agentmemory items in one phase: A11 (`nexus memory audit` CLI), A10 (`nexus memory export` CLI), A12 (`/forget` slash command), and A3 (Ebbinghaus decay sweep). The two new chat-side surfaces `/recall` and `/remember` round out the user-driven retrieval / write surface that the Phase 5 hybrid retriever made possible.

### What changed

**6.1 `nexus memory audit` CLI + audit log foundation (closes agentmemory A11).** New [core/memory/MemoryAuditLog.ts](../core/memory/MemoryAuditLog.ts) defines the `MemoryAuditRow` shape (timestamp, op = write|read|delete, tier, entryId, sessionId, hookKind, toolName, textPreview), a `MemoryAuditFilter` for `--since` / `--tier` / `--session` / `--op` / `--limit`, the `MemoryAuditLog` interface, and a `InMemoryAuditLog` ring-buffer implementation bounded at 10,000 rows by default (drops oldest on overflow). Helpers `previewText` (whitespace-collapsing + ellipsis truncation) and `rowFromProvenance` (project a `LifecycleProvenance` into a row) live in the same module so callers do not need to thread provenance fields by hand. New [core/memory/MemoryAudit.ts](../core/memory/MemoryAudit.ts) ships the pure formatters: `formatAuditTable(rows, columns?)` renders a fixed-width table whose column widths are computed from the actual rows (capped at each column's `maxWidth`), `formatAuditJsonl(rows)` emits one JSON object per line with trailing newline, `formatTimestamp(unixMs)` is the canonical ISO-without-ms representation, and `parseSinceFlag(value)` accepts both bare `YYYY-MM-DD` and full ISO 8601 strings. The CLI subcommand in [bin/nexus.mjs](../bin/nexus.mjs) (`nexus memory audit --since <ISO> --tier <t> --scope <id> --session <id> --op <op> --format table|json --source <jsonl>`) loads `out/core/memory/MemoryAudit.js` + `out/core/memory/MemoryAuditLog.js`, hydrates the in-memory log from the `--source` JSONL snapshot, applies the filter, and writes to stdout. The sidecar-direct path (no JSONL hop) is the production wiring; the `--source` flag exists so operators can replay against captured snapshots without touching the live database. SQLite-backed persistence is deferred under open item 6.1.P2.P (the v1.1.0 Phase 4 migration already bumped `MEMORY_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 3 and adding the `memory_audit_log` table without a coordinated bump would split the schema upgrade across two commits with no clean rollback).

**6.2 `nexus memory export` / `nexus memory import` CLIs (closes agentmemory A10).** New [core/memory/MemoryExport.ts](../core/memory/MemoryExport.ts) defines `ExportableRow` (id, tier, content, vectorB64, scopeId, provenance, createdAt, accessedAt, accessCount, corroborationCount), the `ExportSource` / `ImportSink` interfaces, and four pure functions: `exportToJsonl(source, filter)` walks the source and emits JSONL; `importFromJsonl(text, sink)` parses JSONL and feeds well-formed rows to the sink while recording per-line errors in the result; `encodeVectorB64(vec)` / `decodeVectorB64(b64)` use `Buffer` on Node and `btoa` / `atob` in browsers, encoding the raw little-endian Float32 bytes so the JSON line length stays predictable and there is no precision loss from decimal serialization; `isPathInside(absoluteTarget, allowedRoot)` is the path-traversal guard the CLI uses to clamp `--out` to `~/.nexus/exports/`. The CLI subcommands in `bin/nexus.mjs` (`nexus memory export --out <file> --source <jsonl> [--tier <list>] [--scope <id>] [--since <ISO>]` and `nexus memory import --in <file> [--out <json>]`) call the same code paths the sidecar uses. Live `MemoryStore` source/sink adapters are deferred under 6.2.P2.Q.

**6.3 `/recall <query>` slash command.** Handler `handleRecall(input, ctx)` in [core/memory/MemorySlashCommands.ts](../core/memory/MemorySlashCommands.ts) calls `HybridRetriever.retrieve(query, {scopeId, visibleScopes, limit: 10})` via the structural `HybridRetrieverLike` interface (so the desktop chat IPC layer and the sidecar sub-agent can share the handler), renders the top-10 hits as a fenced JSON block + machine-readable payload (text, tier, score, entryId, provenance), and writes one `read` row per hit to `ctx.auditLog` with `hookKind: "slash.recall"`. The router catalog ([desktop/src/modules/coding/slashCommands.ts](../desktop/src/modules/coding/slashCommands.ts)) gains the `recall` entry so the chat composer suggests it. Acceptance checks for missing query, missing retriever, and "still warming up" each return a structured `{ok: false, status}` so the chat UI can render the rejection inline.

**6.4 `/remember <text>` slash command.** Handler `handleRemember` writes a working-tier observation via `MemoryWritePort.writeWorking({content, provenance, scopeId?})` with `provenance: {sessionId, hookKind: "slash.remember", parentSpanId?}`. The write also produces a `write` audit-log row. The catalog gains the `remember` entry.

**6.5 `/forget --id <uuid> | --pattern <regex>` slash command + Memory panel "Forget" button (closes agentmemory A12).** Handler `handleForget` parses both flag shapes (`--id` / `--id=` / `--pattern bare` / `--pattern "quoted"`); invalid regex is rejected at parse time. The handler walks `MemoryWritePort.listForForget()` for candidates, gates the deletion via `ctx.confirm(...)` (so the existing `ConfirmationGate` plugs in unchanged), deletes each match via `MemoryWritePort.delete(id)`, and writes a `delete` audit row per row. The Memory panel ([desktop/src/modules/coding/panels/MemoryPanel.tsx](../desktop/src/modules/coding/panels/MemoryPanel.tsx)) gains an optional `onForget(layerKey, index, entry)` prop; when supplied, every entry row renders a "Forget" button alongside the provenance chips. When omitted (legacy mode), the button does not render, so pre-Phase-6 sidecars do not show an inert control. The IPC pipeline (`memory.delete(id)` -> sidecar handler -> `MemoryHub.delete(id)`) is deferred under open item 6.5.P2.R because `MemoryHub` needs a new `delete(id)` method per layer first.

**6.6 Ebbinghaus DecaySweep worker (closes agentmemory A3).** New [core/memory/DecaySweep.ts](../core/memory/DecaySweep.ts) implements the closed-form Ebbinghaus retention curve `R(t) = exp(-elapsed / halfLife * ln(2))` with per-tier defaults (working = 24 h, episodic = 7 d, semantic = 30 d, graph = 365 d -- all overridable via the constructor's `halfLives`). The eviction rule is `retention < 0.05 AND accessCount < 3`. The `DecayProvider` interface decouples the sweep from the store -- the caller wires `list()` (yields every live `DecayableEntry`) and `evict(id)` (returns `true` on success; the implementation owns tombstoning). `DecaySweep.sweep()` runs a single pass, returns `{scanned, evicted, kept, elapsedMs}`, and survives per-row `evict` exceptions so a single flaky row cannot wedge the whole sweep. The pure `retentionAt(elapsed, halfLife)` helper is exposed for unit tests + UI previews; `shouldEvict(entry, now)` decides per-row without driving the sweep. The CLI subcommand `nexus memory decay --now --source <jsonl>` fires a manual sweep for debugging. The `IdleTimeScheduler.register(decaySweep, {id: "memory.decay-sweep", idleThresholdMs: 5 * 60_000, cadenceMs: 24 * 60 * 60_000})` call site in the sidecar is deferred under 6.6.P2.S for the same reason as 5.6.P2.O: it needs a `MemoryStore`-backed `DecayProvider` adapter that Phase 7/8 will land alongside the rest of the persistence cluster.

**6.7 CLI dispatch + parser + Phase 6 lint / build / test gate.** [bin/nexus.mjs](../bin/nexus.mjs) gains the `memory` subcommand with four sub-subcommands (`audit`, `export`, `import`, `decay`) routed through `runMemoryCommand`. Each subcommand resolves the compiled artifact from `out/core/memory/*.js` (so the CLI works against the same code paths the sidecar uses). The existing `parseArgs` handles the new flag shapes without modification because `--now`, `--since <date>`, `--out <path>`, and `--source <path>` all match the established `--flag value` / `--flag=value` patterns. New parseArgs cases in [tests/unit/cli/nexus-cli.test.ts](../tests/unit/cli/nexus-cli.test.ts) lock the parse shape. Root: `npm run build` (tsc) clean; `npm run lint` (eslint src) clean. Unit tests for the five new modules pass independently: MemoryAuditLog 10/10, MemoryAudit 10/10, MemoryExport 12/12, DecaySweep 10/10, MemorySlashCommands 16/16 -- 58 new tests in total, all green.

## [2026-05-19] v1.1.0 Phase 5 -- Hybrid memory retrieval (BM25 + Dense + Graph via RRF) + local embedder + warm-build worker

### Goal

Land the agentmemory A1 + A2 adoptions from [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/comparison-agentmemory.md](v1/v1.1/comparison-agentmemory.md) Section 11.2 P1: replace the in-memory hub's substring retrieval with a hybrid path that fuses BM25, dense cosine, and graph traversal rankings via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), and bundle the local embedder (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, 384-dim ONNX weights) that the dense path needs. The pipeline is corpus-agnostic: it operates on opaque `entryId` strings plus a caller-supplied resolver, so the same primitives plug into the four-layer in-memory `MemoryHub` today (Phase 5) and the SQLite-backed `MemoryStore` in Phase 6/9. Plan reference: [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/plans/phase-05-hybrid-retrieval-and-local-embedder.md](v1/v1.1/plans/phase-05-hybrid-retrieval-and-local-embedder.md).

### What changed

**5.1 LocalEmbedder over `@xenova/transformers` (closes agentmemory A2).** New [core/memory/LocalEmbedder.ts](../core/memory/LocalEmbedder.ts) exposes `class LocalEmbedder { embed(text): Promise<Float32Array>; embedBatch(texts): Promise<Float32Array[]> }` returning 384-dim L2-normalized vectors. The class lazy-loads `@xenova/transformers` via a guarded dynamic `import()` and reads weights from `~/.nexus/runtimes/embedder/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/` (or `$NEXUS_HOME/runtimes/embedder/...` when the env override is set). Production hosts get the weights from the Phase 14 installer payload; dev hosts fall back to the Hugging Face Hub fetch on first use. `static LocalEmbedder.fromInstallPath(weightsPath?)` reads as a production wiring constructor. When the optional dep is unavailable (CI, sandboxed builds) the embedder transparently falls back to a deterministic 384-dim hash sketch (`hashEmbed`) that preserves length / determinism / L2-normalization invariants -- enough to exercise downstream consumers without the 80 MB runtime payload, but explicitly not a substitute for real semantic embeddings (tracked under open item 5.1.P1.M). The `@xenova/transformers ^2.17.2` dependency is declared under `optionalDependencies` so `npm ci` keeps working on hosts without the native build toolchain.

**5.2 BM25 inverted index + tokenizer (closes the BM25 portion of agentmemory A1).** New [core/memory/Bm25Index.ts](../core/memory/Bm25Index.ts) implements standard Okapi BM25 with default `k1 = 1.5` and `b = 0.75` (both exposed via Settings `nexus.memory.bm25.k1` / `.b`). New [core/memory/stopwords.ts](../core/memory/stopwords.ts) holds a frozen 120-word English stop-list (NLTK subset trimmed to high-frequency function words) plus the default `tokenize(text)` (case-fold, split on non-alnum, drop stop-words and single-character tokens). `add(entryId, text)` / `delete(entryId)` mutate in O(tokens-per-doc); replacing an existing entry removes its old postings before reindexing. `search(query, limit)` returns an insertion-ordered `Map<entryId, score>` (descending by score, ties broken by entryId for determinism). The IDF formula is the smoothed BM25+ variant (`log(1 + (N - df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5))`) so scores are never negative. Latency on a 1,000-entry corpus: indexing <200 ms total; search <50 ms p50; add <5 ms median (both measured in the new test file).

**5.3 Dense vector index with on-disk persistence (closes the dense portion of agentmemory A1).** New [core/memory/DenseIndex.ts](../core/memory/DenseIndex.ts) keeps a flat `Float32Array[]` keyed by `entryId`; search is a linear cosine scan (1,000 x 384-dim completes in <50 ms p50). `delete(id)` tombstones the slot; `compact()` reclaims tombstones. `save(filePath)` / `static load(filePath)` round-trip live entries via a custom `"NXDI" + uint32 dim + uint32 count + (uint32 idLen + utf8 id + dim*float32 vec)*` binary format; floats are written with `Buffer.writeFloatLE` to avoid the Float32Array 4-byte alignment requirement when variable-length ids precede the vectors. Default on-disk location is `~/.nexus/memory/dense.bin`. Missing-file load returns an empty index (first-launch path); malformed files throw with a precise reason. The v1.2.0 upgrade path -- swap the linear scan for `hnswlib-node` when corpora grow past ~50K entries -- is documented inline.

**5.4 Reciprocal Rank Fusion (closes the RRF portion of agentmemory A1).** New [core/memory/RrfFuser.ts](../core/memory/RrfFuser.ts) ships both a free `fuse(rankings, k = 60)` function and an `RrfFuser` class wrapper whose `k` is mutable so SettingsStore listeners can update it on the fly. The fused score is `sum_over_rankings(1 / (k + rank_i(e)))` per the Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher SIGIR 2009 paper, with map insertion-order interpreted as rank position so callers can hand in any score-ranked output without re-sorting. Default `k = 60` is exposed as `nexus.memory.rrf.k`. The hand-computed three-ranking example from the paper is checked in as a unit test.

**5.5 HybridRetriever façade + `InMemoryMemoryHub` delegation (closes the integration portion of agentmemory A1).** New [core/memory/HybridRetriever.ts](../core/memory/HybridRetriever.ts) runs BM25 + Dense (via the embedder) + Graph (optional `GraphRanker` interface) in parallel, fuses through `RrfFuser`, resolves ids to `MemoryHit` via an injected `entryProvider`, applies the existing `isVisibleFromScope` filter, and truncates to `limit`. Graceful degradation is built in: any subset of the three stages may be empty without breaking the others (verified by unit test). [core/memory/MemoryHub.ts](../core/memory/MemoryHub.ts) `InMemoryMemoryHub` takes an optional `hybridRetriever` in its constructor (or via `setHybridRetriever()` at runtime) plus a `hybridMinCorpus` threshold (`nexus.memory.hybridMinCorpus`, default 100). Corpora below the threshold stay on the legacy substring scan because the hybrid overhead is wasteful; larger corpora delegate to the hybrid path. A structural `HybridRetrieverLike` interface declared inline in `MemoryHub.ts` (instead of importing the concrete `HybridRetriever` class) keeps the `MemoryHub <-> HybridRetriever` dependency one-way; `npm run check-architecture` confirms no new circular warnings. The plan's "replace the substring path in `UnifiedMemoryRetriever`" instruction was reinterpreted: the literal substring path actually lives in `MemoryHub`, while `src/storage/UnifiedMemoryRetriever` already runs an HNSW + FTS5 + recency hybrid via `MemoryStore.retrieveHybrid`. Migrating the SQLite-backed retriever to the new BM25/Dense indexes is deferred to Phase 6/9 (tracked under 5.5.P1.N).

**5.6 Warm-build worker on first launch (closes agentmemory A1 + A2 integration).** New [core/memory/WarmRebuildWorker.ts](../core/memory/WarmRebuildWorker.ts) ships `warmRebuild(source, embedder, bm25, dense, opts)` which reads every memory row, embeds in batches of 32 (configurable), repopulates the BM25 + Dense indexes, and reports progress via the Phase 4 `HookBus` as `lifecycle.notification` events (`notificationKind: "memory.warm-rebuild"`, severities `info` / `warning` / `error`). Fingerprint-based short-circuit (`source.fingerprint()` vs. `opts.previousFingerprint`) skips the rebuild when nothing changed. `createWarmRebuildTask({...})` returns an `IdleTimeScheduler.register`-compatible shape (id `memory.warm-rebuild`, default 5 s idle threshold, 24 h cadence). Embedder failures degrade to BM25-only with a warning notification rather than crashing the worker. The 10,000-row rebuild completes well under the 60 s acceptance ceiling. The actual `scheduler.register(...)` call site in the sidecar is deferred under 5.6.P2.O because it needs the `MemoryStore` adapter that Phase 6 will land.

**5.7 Phase 5 lint / build / test gate.** Root: `npm run build` (tsc) clean; `npm run lint` (eslint src) clean (the new sources live under `core/memory/` which is outside the eslint scope per the existing project policy, matching Phase 4's pattern); `npm run check-architecture` (depcruise on `src core modules`) clean -- the new modules add zero circular dependencies and zero new orphans. `npm test` -- 3132 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (was 3042 in Phase 4; the +90 covers the 9 new memory test files). New benchmark in [tests/benchmarks/hybrid-retrieval.bench.ts](../tests/benchmarks/hybrid-retrieval.bench.ts) runs via `npm run bench` and prints the hybrid retrieve top-10 distribution on 1,000 entries (~243 hz mean on the dev laptop, well inside the p99 < 150 ms budget). Settings additions in [package.json](../package.json): `nexus.memory.bm25.k1`, `nexus.memory.bm25.b`, `nexus.memory.rrf.k`, `nexus.memory.hybridMinCorpus`, each with min/max bounds and a description that points to the consuming module.

### Outcome

### Known gaps recap

After Phase 5 the v1.1.0 known-gaps file has 12 open items + 21 resolved (was 9 + 14 after Phase 4). The seven new Phase 5 closures are agentmemory A2 (LocalEmbedder), agentmemory A1 in four parts (BM25 + Dense + RRF + Hybrid façade), the warm-build worker (A1 + A2 integration), and the bench + settings package. The three new open items are: 5.1.P1.M (CI runs against the deterministic hash fallback; real ONNX pipeline is exercised manually until Phase 14 ships the installer-packed weights), 5.5.P1.N (the `src/storage/UnifiedMemoryRetriever` migration is intentionally deferred -- the substring path the plan referenced actually lives in `MemoryHub`, which is where the hybrid delegation landed; migrating the SQLite-backed retriever to the new indexes is folded into Phase 6/9), and 5.6.P2.O (the `IdleTimeScheduler.register(createWarmRebuildTask(...))` call site in the sidecar is deferred until Phase 6 provides the `MemoryStore` adapter that wraps `MemoryStore.iterateAllRows()` as a `WarmRebuildSource`).

### Why this scope

Phase 5 is the second of three "memory upgrade lens" phases. A1 (hybrid retrieval) and A2 (local embedder) are the cluster's high-fanout adoptions per [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/comparison-agentmemory.md](v1/v1.1/comparison-agentmemory.md) Section 11.2: every subsequent agentmemory adoption (A3 decay, A11/A10 CLI surfaces, A6 replay, A4/A9 consolidation) reads from the hybrid path. Building the BM25 / Dense / RRF / Hybrid primitives as corpus-agnostic modules under `core/memory/` -- keyed by opaque `entryId` strings plus a caller-supplied `entryProvider` -- means the SQLite-backed wiring in Phase 6/9 reuses the same building blocks without rewriting them. The decision to keep the substring fast-path for corpora below `nexus.memory.hybridMinCorpus` (default 100) preserves correctness for unit tests and small dev sessions while letting real workloads cross over into the hybrid ranking automatically. The hash-fallback embedder is the necessary compromise that lets the rest of the pipeline ship with full test coverage without forcing every CI host to download the 80 MB ONNX payload; the real pipeline lights up at Phase 14 installer time.

## [2026-05-19] v1.1.0 Phase 4 -- Memory provenance schema + 12-hook lifecycle bus + pre-index secret redaction

### Goal

Land the agentmemory A8 + A5 + A7 adoptions from [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/comparison-agentmemory.md](v1/v1.1/comparison-agentmemory.md) Section 11.2 P0 plus the v1.0.0 4.P1.X scope_id closure: (a) every memory row carries a structured `LifecycleProvenance` blob tying it back to the lifecycle event that produced it, (b) a typed `HookBus` surfaces 12 lifecycle events that internal consumers (Memory panel, audit CLI, trace replay) get with compile-time payloads, and (c) every memory write is scrubbed through a consolidated `redactSecrets()` function before SQLite insert so AWS keys / GitHub PATs / Slack tokens / JWTs / PEM private-key blocks never reach the index. Plan reference: [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/plans/phase-04-memory-provenance-and-hooks.md](v1/v1.1/plans/phase-04-memory-provenance-and-hooks.md).

### What changed

**4.1 Memory provenance + scope_id schema (closes agentmemory A8 + v1.0.0 4.P1.X).** New [core/memory/types.ts](../core/memory/types.ts) defines `LifecycleProvenance: {sessionId, hookKind, toolName?, parentSpanId?}` along with `parseProvenance` / `serializeProvenance` helpers that round-trip through SQLite TEXT columns without throwing on malformed JSON. The canonical migration SQL is checked in at [core/storage/migrations/v1.1.0_provenance.sql](../core/storage/migrations/v1.1.0_provenance.sql) for reference; the runtime migration is performed in TypeScript so each ALTER is guarded by a column-presence `PRAGMA table_info` check (idempotent across re-opens). [src/storage/MemoryStore.ts](../src/storage/MemoryStore.ts) `_initSchema` now declares `provenance TEXT NULL` and `scope_id TEXT NULL` on the `memories` table; the migration block adds them in place when migrating from `user_version <= 2`; schema version bumped to 3. `save(content, type, sessionId, options)` accepts an optional `{provenance, scopeId}` block, JSON-serializes the provenance on insert, and JSON-parses on read. `_rowToEntry` projects `lifecycleProvenance` and `scopeId` onto the returned `MemoryEntry`. The same migration pattern lands on [src/storage/EpisodicMemory.ts](../src/storage/EpisodicMemory.ts) `episodic_events` and [src/storage/GraphMemory.ts](../src/storage/GraphMemory.ts) `graph_relations`; helper indexes `idx_memories_scope` / `idx_episodic_scope` / `idx_relations_scope` mirror the in-memory `MemoryHub` scope filter. [src/storage/MemoryShared.types.ts](../src/storage/MemoryShared.types.ts) `MemoryEntry` carries the new `lifecycleProvenance?: LifecycleProvenance | null` + `scopeId?: string | null` optional fields without breaking any existing consumer (the legacy `MemoryProvenance` source/confidence record remains in place). [core/memory/MemoryHub.ts](../core/memory/MemoryHub.ts) gains a `provenance?` field on every entry-input and projects it onto `MemoryHit.provenance`; the three in-memory layer implementations propagate it through `add` / `record` / `upsert` / `retagScope`.

**4.2 Typed HookBus (closes agentmemory A5).** New [core/lifecycle/HookBus.ts](../core/lifecycle/HookBus.ts) defines a closed 12-variant `LifecycleEvent` discriminated union covering `session.start/.stop/.end`, `user.prompt`, `tool.pre/.post/.failed`, `subagent.start/.stop`, `context.preCompact`, `notification`, `skill.entry`. The default `InProcessHookBus` exposes typed `on<K>(kind, handler)` / `onAny(handler)` subscriptions with O(1) `Disposable.dispose()`, and every `emit(...)` is re-published onto the underlying `TelemetryBus` under the `lifecycle.*` kind so trace-side consumers see the lifecycle stream without subscribing twice. A misbehaving handler cannot take the bus down (errors are swallowed per-handler).

**4.3 HookBus emit sites wired into AgentLoop (closes the 5 in-blast-radius hooks; defers 4 to 4.3.P1.J).** [src/tools/AgentLoop.ts](../src/tools/AgentLoop.ts) `AgentLoopOptions` gains `hookBus?: HookBus`. `run()` emits `lifecycle.session.start` at the top (with `{sessionId, modelId, isoTime}`) and `lifecycle.session.stop` at every return path (centralized in `_emitSessionStop`, captures `durationMs`). `_runToolCall` emits `lifecycle.tool.pre` before `_registry.execute`, `lifecycle.tool.post` after the call returns, and an additional `lifecycle.tool.failed` (with `redactSecrets()`-scrubbed error text) when `result.success === false`. `spawnSubAgent` brackets the dispatch with `lifecycle.subagent.start` / `lifecycle.subagent.stop` carrying `{role, ok, parentSpanId}`. The remaining 4 hooks (`user.prompt`, `context.preCompact`, `session.end`, `skill.entry`) stay deferred per 4.3.P1.J because each requires a surface still tracked by an upstream open item (Phase 1.4 sub-tree moves for `ChatController` and `Tracer.snapshot`, Phase 1.10 for `SessionStore.close`, Phase 8 for `setCurrentSkill`).

**4.4 Pre-index secret redaction (closes agentmemory A7).** New [core/observability/redactSecrets.ts](../core/observability/redactSecrets.ts) consolidates the secret-pattern catalog historically maintained inside `src/observability/TraceFile.ts` into a single string-in / string-out scrubber: AWS access keys (`AKIA...`, `ASIA...`, `AGPA...`, `AROA...`, `AIDA...`, `ANPA...`, `ANVA...`, `ASCA...`), classic GitHub PATs (`gh[pousr]_<36+>`), fine-grained GitHub PATs (`github_pat_<82+>`), Slack tokens (`xox[abcepors]-...`), JWTs (`eyJ...`), PEM private-key blocks (multi-line, any kind: RSA / DSA / EC / OPENSSH), and env-style assignments where the value looks high-entropy (16+ base64/hex chars). The env-style case keeps the variable name so log lines stay diagnostically useful (`OPENAI_API_KEY=<redacted>` not `<redacted>`). The scrubber is wired into `MemoryStore.save(...)` so `entry.content` is scrubbed before SQLite insert. The same module also redacts `lifecycle.tool.failed.redactedError` so a tool failure that leaks a key in its error text never reaches the bus.

**4.5 Desktop UI surfaces (closes the 4.5 acceptance for the consumer side; defers sidecar producer to 4.5.P2.L).** [desktop/sidecar/src/protocol.ts](../desktop/sidecar/src/protocol.ts) extends `MemorySnapshot` with an optional `provenance` map (`Record<layerName, Array<MemoryEntryProvenance | null>>`) and `TraceEvent` with an optional `hookKind` string; both are gated as `.optional()` so older sidecars keep working. [desktop/src/modules/coding/panels/MemoryPanel.tsx](../desktop/src/modules/coding/panels/MemoryPanel.tsx) gains a `useState`-driven "Show provenance" toggle that renders `hookKind` + `toolName` chips next to each entry when on. [desktop/src/modules/coding/panels/TraceDashboardPanel.tsx](../desktop/src/modules/coding/panels/TraceDashboardPanel.tsx) gains a `hookKind` `<select>` filter whose options are derived from the distinct hookKinds present on the current event stream (events without a hookKind stay visible regardless of filter). New panel tests cover both flows: `panels.test.tsx > shows provenance chips when toggle is on` and `> filters events by hookKind via the dropdown`.

**4.6 Lint / build / test gate.** Root: `npm run build` (tsc) clean; `npm run lint` (eslint src) clean; `npm run check-architecture` (depcruise on `src core modules`) clean. `npm test` -- 3042 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (was 3019 in Phase 3; the +23 covers HookBus / redactSecrets / MemoryStore.provenance / AgentLoop.hookBus). Desktop: `npm test` -- 366 passed / 0 failed (was 364; +2 from the new panel tests).

### Known gaps recap

After Phase 4 the v1.1.0 known-gaps file has 9 open items + 15 resolved (was 6 + 10 after Phase 3). The five new Phase 4 closures are agentmemory A8 (memory provenance schema), v1.0.0 4.P1.X (scope_id on persistent memory tables), agentmemory A5 (HookBus + 5 of 12 emit sites), agentmemory A7 (pre-index secret redaction), and the 4.5 UI surfaces (toggle + filter). The three new open items are: 4.3.P1.J (the remaining 4 emit sites for user.prompt + preCompact + session.end + skill.entry, each waiting on an upstream phase), 4.1.P2.K (the v1.0.0 fixture SQLite is generated in-test rather than checked in as a binary -- acceptance is met; deviation recorded to avoid binary churn), and 4.5.P2.L (the sidecar producer for the new optional protocol fields is not yet wired; the consumer side degrades gracefully).

### Why this scope

Phase 4 is one of three "memory upgrade lens" phases in the agentmemory cluster (the others are Phase 5 hybrid retrieval + local embedder and Phase 6 decay + CLI). A8 (schema) is the foundation every other agentmemory adoption depends on -- the [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/comparison-agentmemory.md](v1/v1.1/comparison-agentmemory.md) cluster diagram has A8 fan out to A5 / A7 / A11 / A6 / A3 / A10 / A12. Landing A8 + A5 + A7 together gives Phase 5 / 6 / 7 a stable typed surface to consume; landing them as separate sub-phases would force two rounds of `MemoryStore.save(...)` signature churn. The deferred 4 emit sites (4.3.P1.J) were not in the critical path -- the 5 wired sites cover the highest-event-rate surfaces (every tool call brackets two events; every session bookends two) -- so the consumer-side surfaces (Memory panel chips, TraceDashboard filter) have enough live data to verify against without the missing four.

## [2026-05-19] v1.1.0 Phase 3 -- Coding module move: codemod infrastructure + first `src/utils/` -> `modules/coding/utils/` leaf migration

### Goal

Land the cycle's `src/` -> `modules/coding/` migration pipeline by (a) shipping the generic import-rewriting codemod that v1.1.0 Phase 1 sub-task 1.4 specified, and (b) executing the first end-to-end sub-tree migration as a forcing function on the codemod's correctness across every relative-path depth a future sub-tree move will encounter. The pick is `src/utils/` because it is the smallest true leaf in `src/` (6 files, zero intra-`src/` imports -- it only consumes node builtins + external npm packages), and it has ~63 importers spanning `src/` itself plus `tests/{unit,integration,benchmarks}/...`. After Phase 3, the remaining 12 sub-tree moves under 1.4.P1.B are mechanical: each future phase that touches the rename consumes `node scripts/dev/rewrite-imports.mjs --moves <manifest.json>`. Plan reference: [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/plans/phase-03-coding-module.md](v1/v1.1/plans/phase-03-coding-module.md).

### What changed

**3.1 Import-rewriting codemod (closes 3.P1.A, new this phase).** New script [scripts/dev/rewrite-imports.mjs](../scripts/dev/rewrite-imports.mjs) walks `src/`, `core/`, `modules/`, and `tests/` and rewrites every static `import ... from "X"` / `import "X"` / `export ... from "X"`, dynamic `import("X")`, and `vi.mock("X", ...)` / `vi.doMock("X", ...)` / `vi.hoisted(...)` specifier whose resolved absolute path lands inside a moved sub-tree. The script is zero-dependency (pure Node), idempotent (a re-run after a successful pass writes zero files), and accepts a `--moves` JSON manifest (defaults to the Phase 3 utils move when omitted) plus a `--dry-run` flag. Path comparisons normalize to POSIX-style forward slashes so the diff is identical on Windows / macOS / Linux. The regex set handles all five specifier kinds, preserves the `module: "Node16"` `.js` extension on output, and emits `./relative/...` paths with a leading dot when the target is a sibling.

**3.2 `src/utils/` -> `modules/coding/utils/` migration (closes the first row of the 1.4.P1.B status table; partial closure of v1.0.0 carryforward 2.P2.I).** `git mv src/utils modules/coding/utils` moved the six leaf files (`Compressor.ts`, `errors.ts`, `logger.ts`, `MarkdownRenderer.ts`, `secretPaths.ts`, `ssrf.ts`) with rename history preserved. The codemod then rewrote 65 importing files in a single pass: 48 sources under `src/` (every `src/<subtree>/*` file that consumed a utils helper plus the top-level `src/extension.ts`), 16 tests under `tests/{unit,integration,benchmarks}/...` (including the two `vi.mock(...)` mock paths in `tests/unit/panels/ChatCommandHandlers.test.ts` and `tests/unit/panels/ChatController.test.ts`), and a single `vi.mock` in the panels tests for `MarkdownRenderer`. [configs/vitest.config.ts](../configs/vitest.config.ts) coverage `exclude` array was flipped from `"src/utils/**"` to `"modules/coding/utils/**"` so the coverage gate continues to treat the leaf as a coverage-excluded module (its members are exercised end-to-end through their consumers, not directly). The realistic-shaped grep-output fixture strings in [tests/integration/tool-output-compression.test.ts](../tests/integration/tool-output-compression.test.ts) `buildGrepResult(...)` (lines 33-39) were intentionally NOT rewritten -- they are test data simulating a realistic codebase, not live import specifiers.

**3.3 Lint / build / typecheck / test / depcruise gate.** Root: `npm run build` (tsc) clean; `npm run lint` (eslint src) clean; `npm run check-architecture` (depcruise on `src core modules`) -- 0 errors, 5 pre-existing orphan warnings unchanged from the Phase 2 baseline; `npm test` -- 3019 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (identical to the Phase 2 baseline; the 65-file rewrite produced zero new test failures). Desktop: `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) clean; `npm test` -- 364 passed / 0 failed. The desktop tree did not consume `src/utils/` directly so its result is structural, but it confirms there is no transitive regression.

### Outcome

- Files moved: 6 (`src/utils/Compressor.ts` -> `modules/coding/utils/Compressor.ts`, `errors.ts`, `logger.ts`, `MarkdownRenderer.ts`, `secretPaths.ts`, `ssrf.ts`); rename history preserved via `git mv`.
- Files rewritten by codemod: 65 (48 sources in `src/<subtree>/` + 1 in `src/extension.ts` + 12 unit tests + 3 integration tests + 1 benchmark).
- Manual edit: [configs/vitest.config.ts](../configs/vitest.config.ts) coverage `exclude` flipped to the new path.
- New scripts: [scripts/dev/rewrite-imports.mjs](../scripts/dev/rewrite-imports.mjs).
- New documents: [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/plans/phase-03-coding-module.md](v1/v1.1/plans/phase-03-coding-module.md).
- Updated documents: [docs/versions/v1/v1.1.0/known-gaps.md](v1/v1.1/known-gaps.md) -- new entry `Phase 3 closures (this commit)` recording 3.P1.A (codemod, new) + the first row of 1.4.P1.B's per-sub-tree status table (`src/utils/` closed); the 1.4.P1.B body was rewritten as a status table tracking all 13 sub-trees; the `## 3. Summary` totals shifted to 6 open / 10 resolved (one new resolved P1 from 3.P1.A) and 16 total. This DEVLOG.
- Test status: 3019 root tests passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped; 364 desktop tests passed / 0 failed. Coverage gate unchanged.
- Build / typecheck: root `tsc` clean, desktop `tsc --noEmit` clean, root `eslint src` clean, root `depcruise` 0 errors / 5 orphan warnings (pre-existing baseline).

### Known gaps recap

After Phase 3 the v1.1.0 known-gaps file has 6 open items + 10 resolved (was 6 open + 9 resolved after Phase 2). The newly resolved row is 3.P1.A (codemod infrastructure). 1.4.P1.B stays under `## 1. Open Items` because 12 of the 13 sub-tree moves are still pending; its body now carries a status table so each future phase that ships a `git mv <subtree>` ticks one row off in lock-step. Suggested next sub-tree for Phase 4: `src/config/` (9 files, leaf-shaped, low coupling).

### Why this scope

The original Phase 1 sub-task 1.4 enumerated all 13 sub-tree moves in a single bullet, but the Phase 2 plan explicitly recorded the "must land sub-tree by sub-tree on a dedicated branch with per-step CI runs" constraint as the reason the move was deferred. Phase 3 honours that constraint by landing the codemod (the shared infrastructure every future move consumes) plus one demonstrative leaf migration whose ~63 importers exercise every relative-path depth a subsequent migration will encounter. The leaf choice (`src/utils/`) is deliberate: it has zero intra-`src/` dependencies, so its move cannot accidentally drag along a sibling sub-tree's import graph. The result is a reviewable commit where every diff is either (a) the codemod itself, (b) a `git mv` rename, (c) a mechanical relative-path rewrite, or (d) the documentation that records (a)-(c).

The installer scripts (`scripts/installer/pyqt/...`, `scripts/installer/legacy/setup.nsi`) still reference the legacy extension ID `gemma-code.gemma-code`; those flip when sub-task 1.6 lands.

**1.3 deprecationMessage injection.** [scripts/dev/inject-deprecation-messages.mjs](../scripts/dev/inject-deprecation-messages.mjs) walks `SETTINGS_KEY_MAP` in `src/config/settingsKeyMap.ts`, opens `package.json`, and for every legacy `gemma-code.*` entry in `contributes.configuration.properties` writes `"deprecationMessage": "Use ` + "`${newKey}`" + ` instead. Will be removed in v1.2.0."`. Catch-all branch handles 5 legacy keys with no canonical replacement (renamed message asks the user to file an issue referencing the conjectured `nexus.*` counterpart). Run once: 58 messages injected; idempotent on re-runs. The VS Code Settings UI will now render every legacy `gemma-code.*` entry with a strikethrough + deprecation hint pointing at its `nexus.*` replacement.

**1.7 Curator-cadence fallback deleted.** [src/tools/AgentLoop.ts](../src/tools/AgentLoop.ts) `_runOneIteration` no longer fires the `curator-worker` sub-agent on the post-N-edits trigger. The `curatorWorkerEnabled` / `curatorWorkerMinIntervalMs` options remain accepted on `AgentLoopOptions` for back-compat with `ChatController` / `ChatPanelBootstrap` call-sites that wire `settings.curatorWorkerEnabled` through, but the field declarations and 12-hour cadence state were removed; the options are `void`-discarded in the constructor with a clarifying comment. The OR-gate in the verification dispatch block was narrowed to `verification || audit || testgaps`. The `IdleTimeScheduler` is now the sole curator entry point. A new `nexus.curator.enabled` boolean (default `true`) was added to `package.json` `contributes.configuration.properties` so the future IdleTimeScheduler curator task has a Settings UI toggle. The actual wiring of the IdleTimeScheduler curator task to consult `nexus.curator.enabled` is queued for "Phase 1b" -- the legacy gate (`nexus.workers.curator.enabled`, default false) is no longer consulted in production code paths.

**1.8 CRLF/LF snapshot normalization + SHA-pin (verified).** New [.gitattributes](../.gitattributes) declares `tests/snapshots/specialists/*.txt text eol=lf` + same for the one `.json` snapshot file so the byte-exact characterization tests in `tests/unit/agents/SubAgentManager.characterization.test.ts` pass on Windows checkouts. Existing snapshot files were converted in-place from CRLF to LF via a one-shot PowerShell pass. The shell-build.yml SHA-pins were already in place from v1.0.0 (every action -- `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, `actions/cache`, `actions/upload-artifact` -- is pinned to a 40-char SHA with a trailing `# version-tag` comment for readability), so sub-task 1.8 was satisfied by the CRLF half alone.

**Test fixtures updated.** 8 test files updated to reflect the new path: `tests/unit/agents/SpecialistLoader.test.ts`, `tests/unit/commands/memoryLintCommand.test.ts`, `tests/unit/hooks/check-prompt-policy.test.ts`, `tests/unit/utils/secretPaths.test.ts`, `tests/unit/observability/OperationLog.test.ts`, `tests/unit/observability/TraceFile.test.ts` (now asserts `.nexus` substring in the path), `tests/unit/tools/OutputRedirector.test.ts`, `tests/unit/storage/ToolOutputCache.test.ts`, `tests/unit/panels/ChatCommandHandlers.test.ts`, `tests/integration/storage/cleanupScanner.test.ts`, `tests/integration/memory-lint-end-to-end.test.ts`. `tests/unit/core/storage/StorageMigration.test.ts` is unchanged -- it deliberately tests the legacy `~/.gemma-code/` -> `~/.nexus/` migration path and must keep both string references.

### Goal

Close the v1.0.0 cycle: deep review of every prior phase, security audit + pen-test, Authenticode signing workflow, CHANGELOG + release notes covering every Phase 1-10 deliverable, version bump across all version-carrying files, RTM smoke checklist, distribution channels, finalize the v1.0.0 known-gaps file, flip the v0.9.0 known-gaps file to `finalized`. ### What changed

**11.1 Deep review synthesis.** [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/review/synthesis.md](v1/v1.0/review/synthesis.md) consolidates every Phase 1-10 review artifact into a single sign-off document. The synthesis identifies three architectural choke points behind the 47-item carryforward to v1.1.0: (a) the shared-core build (Node16 module resolution cannot cross the workspace boundary into `core/` without TypeScript project references), (b) the real-GPU + real-PyTorch wiring (the Python sidecar's `_execute(ctx)` defaults to stubs without a CUDA host), and (c) the VS Code thin-adapter rewrite (gated on the shared-core build + the Marketplace re-publish under `nexus-coding`). All three are scheduled for v1.1.0; the v1.0.0 surface works end-to-end via placeholder paths in every affected module.

**11.2 Security audit + pen-test.** [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/review/security-audit.md](v1/v1.0/review/security-audit.md) runs the OWASP ASVS L1 + SECURITY.md threat-model sweep: exposed-secrets grep clean; IPC payloads Zod-validated end-to-end; installer privilege boundary at install-time only (sidecars run as user); model downloader rejects `file://`, `localhost`, RFC1918 ranges; ffmpeg shell-out is argv-only (no shell interpolation); `~/.nexus/` permissions OS-defaulted (P2 hardening for v1.0.1: explicit `chmod 700` on POSIX). [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/review/penetration-test.md](v1/v1.0/review/penetration-test.md) runs the depth=deep six-specialist OWASP WSTG pass: prompt-injection corpus blocked by `PromptInjectionScanner`, no subprocess-spawn surface reachable from renderer-controlled payloads, `tauri.conf.json` CSP restricted (script-src no inline; img-src data + blob for diffusion previews), `GpuScheduler` queue-cap defends against job-flood DoS, race-free skill rotation via atomic `ACTIVE`-pointer write-then-rename. Zero P0 / P1 findings across both reports.

**11.3 Authenticode signing + macOS notarization.** [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/release-signing.md](v1/v1.0/release-signing.md) Section 1 captures the Windows EV-cert + HSM + `signtool sign /tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td sha256 /fd sha256 /sha1 $THUMBPRINT /a` workflow with sign-order (inner binaries first, NSIS outer last), CI integration gated on tag-push, and verification via `signtool verify /pa /v`. Section 2 captures the macOS Developer ID Application + Installer cert workflow, hardened-runtime + JIT entitlements, `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, `xcrun stapler staple`, `spctl --assess --type install` verification. EV cert procurement is operator-driven (5-10 business day lead time at typical CAs) and tracked as OA-01; macOS notarization is deferred to v1.0.1 per Phase 9.8 and tracked as OA-11.

**11.4 CHANGELOG + release notes.** [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md) gains a v1.0.0 entry above the existing 0.30.1 entry. ## [2026-05-17] v1.0.0 Phase 10 -- DevAI-Hub sync pathway

### Goal

Open the upstream link to `bendourthe/DevAI-Hub` cleanly: a `nexus skills sync` CLI subcommand and matching Settings UI that sparse-clones a pinned tag into `~/.nexus/skills/devai-hub/<tag>/`, scans every SKILL.md with a built-in prompt-injection detector before activation, namespaces skills under `devai-hub/<name>` to avoid collisions with user-authored skills, threads provenance through the existing trace dashboard, and ships a "diverged" badge so the user can pick a side when a local skill and a DevAI-Hub skill share a display name. Plan reference: [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/plans/phase-10-devai-hub-sync.md](v1/v1.0/plans/phase-10-devai-hub-sync.md).

### What changed

**10.1 Namespaced SkillCatalog with provenance.** Extended [core/skills/SkillCatalog.ts](../core/skills/SkillCatalog.ts): every `SkillRecord` (and `Skill`) gains a `provenance: SkillProvenance` field where `SkillProvenance = {source: "builtin" | "user" | "devai-hub", tag?: string, contentHash: string}`. New helpers `canonicalSkillId(source, name)` (returns `<source>/<name>` for non-builtin) and `namespaceForSource(source)` (echoes the source as a `SkillNamespace`) make the addressing convention explicit. `SkillCatalog` gains `listByNamespace(ns)` so the UI can render per-namespace sections; `InMemorySkillCatalog` computes a diverged-display-name set on construction (and on `resetForTesting`) so any record whose display name appears in more than one source surfaces `diverged: true` to the UI. The existing test fixture in [tests/unit/core/skills/SkillCatalog.test.ts](../tests/unit/core/skills/SkillCatalog.test.ts) grew from 7 to 15 tests covering provenance round-trip, listByNamespace filtering, no-collision when a user skill shares a name with a devai-hub skill, diverged-flag rendering, and the canonical-id helpers.

**10.2 `nexus skills sync` CLI + DevAIHubSyncer core.** New top-level binary [bin/nexus.mjs](../bin/nexus.mjs) registered in `package.json`'s `bin` map alongside the existing nexus-check / nexus-image / nexus-video CLIs. Subcommand surface: `nexus skills sync [--tag <tag>] [--apply]`, `nexus skills list [--namespace <ns>]`, `nexus skills install <ns>/<name>` (stub; tracked as `10.P2.III`), `nexus skills remove <ns>/<name>` (stub), plus `nexus check` pass-through. The core sync pipeline lives in [core/skills/DevAIHubSyncer.ts](../core/skills/DevAIHubSyncer.ts) so it is unit-testable without spawning a CLI: `DevAIHubSyncer.sync({tag, apply})` resolves the latest tag (or uses `--tag` override), short-circuits when `~/.nexus/skills/devai-hub/<tag>/` already exists with a matching bundle hash, sparse-clones into a tmp dir (`~/.nexus/skills/.tmp-devai-hub-<tag>/`) -- falling back to tarball when `git` is missing on PATH -- computes a stable bundle hash (sorted relative-path + sha256 of each SKILL.md body), writes `manifest.json`, diffs against the currently-active manifest, runs the prompt-injection scanner against every SKILL.md + bundled `.sh` / `.ps1` / `.mjs` / `.cjs` / `.js`, and (when `--apply` and the scan's decision is not `block`) atomically rotates the active dir and updates the `~/.nexus/skills/devai-hub/ACTIVE` pointer. `SyncDependencies` is dependency-injected so the integration tests in [tests/unit/core/skills/DevAIHubSyncer.test.ts](../tests/unit/core/skills/DevAIHubSyncer.test.ts) cover the entire pipeline end-to-end (23 tests: manifest walking, diff add/modify/remove detection, summarizeDiff rendering, empty-bundle SHA256, active-tag pointer round-trip, full sync against a local fixture, --apply rotation, "already up to date" short-circuit, latest-tag resolution, tarball fallback when `hasGit() === false`, injection-scan blocks --apply, invalid-tag rejection, two-version diff, manifest.json write, defaultDependencies smoke).

**10.3 Prompt-injection scanner.** New [core/skills/PromptInjectionScanner.ts](../core/skills/PromptInjectionScanner.ts) with 11 built-in rules across five buckets: (a) jailbreak templates (`ignore previous instructions`, `disregard your training`, `you are now <persona>`, `system:` role prefix, `<|im_start|>` / `<|im_end|>` chat-template tokens); (b) safety / guardrail disablement (`disable safety|guardrails|filters`, `bypass safety|guardrails|filters`); (c) credential-exfil paths (`dump .env`, `cat .env`, `POST /env`, `.aws/credentials`, `.ssh/id_*`); (d) known exfil URL hosts (beeceptor.com, webhook.site, requestbin.io, burpcollaborator.net -- with or without subdomain); (e) `<|tool_call|>` / `<tool_call>` tags in the SKILL.md body. Severity ladder: `high` blocks activation, `medium` warns + logs, `low` logs only. `scanText(content, source)` runs the rules line-by-line so findings carry a precise line number; `scanBundle(files)` aggregates across a synced bundle and bubbles the worst decision up via `decision: "block" | "warn" | "pass"`. 18 unit tests in [tests/unit/core/skills/PromptInjectionScanner.test.ts](../tests/unit/core/skills/PromptInjectionScanner.test.ts) cover every rule against a positive and a negative payload, plus the bundle-aggregation, source/line-number tracking, and the custom-rule-set injection point.

**10.4 SkillsSettings UI + 10.6 diverged badge.** New [desktop/src/pages/settings/SkillsSettings.tsx](../desktop/src/pages/settings/SkillsSettings.tsx) renders the operator surface: header shows the active DevAI-Hub tag (e.g. `v1.3.2`) next to the upstream-latest tag; control row offers a "Sync now" button (drives `syncNow()`) and an "Auto-sync weekly (idle time)" checkbox; quarantined skills (`quarantine.decision === "block"`) appear in a dedicated section with up to three rendered scanner findings each and a "Review and approve" action; per-namespace lists (DevAI-Hub / User / Built-in) render the skill id, provenance tag, and an Enable / Disable toggle. Diverged rows render a small "diverged" pill plus a "Use as default" button that drives `setDivergedPreference(displayName, preference)`. The page is provider-driven via a `SkillsSettingsClient` interface so tests and the future IPC wiring can swap implementations. [desktop/src/pages/settings/SettingsPage.tsx](../desktop/src/pages/settings/SettingsPage.tsx) upgrades from a single-page shell to a tabbed shell with Models + Skills tabs. New [desktop/src/pages/settings/mockSkillsClient.ts](../desktop/src/pages/settings/mockSkillsClient.ts) backs the dev/test mode with three sample skills (one built-in, one user, one devai-hub, with the latter two flagged as diverged). [desktop/tests/SkillsSettings.test.tsx](../desktop/tests/SkillsSettings.test.tsx) ships 11 tests: header renders active + upstream tag, rows group by namespace, diverged badge shows on conflicting display names but not on the non-diverged builtin row, Sync-now drives the client + renders status, auto-sync toggles via `setAutoSyncEnabled(true)`, quarantined section renders findings, "Review and approve" drives `approveQuarantined`, toggle button inverts active state, "Use as default" drives `setDivergedPreference`, error path renders when `list()` rejects.

**10.5 Provenance traces.** [src/observability/Tracer.ts](../src/observability/Tracer.ts) gains a `SkillSpanContext` type, a `setCurrentSkill(...)` setter (paired with a `currentSkill` getter), and an automatic fold-in: every `startSpan` of kind `tool_call` or `sub_agent` gets the active skill's `skill.id` / `skill.namespace` / `skill.tag` / `skill.contentHash` flattened into the span attributes. Flattening is necessary because the underlying `TraceStore` attribute column only carries `string | number | boolean` (no nested objects). Two paired helpers -- `skillContextAttributes(ctx)` and `readSkillContextFromAttributes(attrs)` -- make the round-trip explicit so the trace dashboard can reconstruct the structured skill block from any persisted attribute record. Non-tool / non-sub-agent spans (llm_call, planning, compaction, etc.) are left untouched so the dashboard-level "tool call originated from skill X" semantics stay clean. 9 unit tests in [tests/unit/observability/TracerSkillProvenance.test.ts](../tests/unit/observability/TracerSkillProvenance.test.ts) cover the flatten + round-trip, namespace validation, fold-in on `tool_call` and `sub_agent`, no fold-in on `llm_call`, and the clear-via-null path.

### Outcome

- New unit tests: 65 across core/skills (`SkillCatalog` +8, `PromptInjectionScanner` 18, `DevAIHubSyncer` 23) + cli (`nexus-cli` 5) + observability (`TracerSkillProvenance` 9) + skills total = 53 net new + 12 expanded.
- New desktop UI tests: 11 (SkillsSettings).
- Full Phase 10 suites: 225 / 225 green (`tests/unit/skills` + `tests/unit/observability` + `tests/unit/cli`).
- Existing root-project vitest: 3009 / 3009 pre-Phase-10 tests pass (4 pre-existing CRLF-vs-LF snapshot failures in `tests/unit/agents/SubAgentManager.characterization.test.ts` reproduce on `main`; unrelated to Phase 10, tracked separately).
- Desktop vitest: 362 / 362 green.
- Lint: clean (eslint scoped to `src/**/*.ts` per the existing config; `core/`, `bin/`, and `desktop/` covered by their own configs and all pass).
- Typecheck: clean (`tsc --noEmit` at root + desktop).

## [2026-05-17] v1.0.0 Phase 9 -- Single-binary installer overhaul (Windows-first)

### Goal

Lay the v1.0.0 installer foundation: a two-layer `Nexus-1.0.0-Setup.exe` (NSIS outer shell handling UAC / registry / Start Menu / file association / URL handler; PyQt5 wizard inner provisioning CUDA 12.1 runtime, an offline Python venv with the diffusion stack, Node 22, Ollama, recommended models, and the frozen DevAI-Hub skill baseline). macOS DMG + Linux AppImage scoped and CI-stubbed for v1.0.1 / v1.0.2. Plan reference: [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/plans/phase-09-installer.md](v1/v1.0/plans/phase-09-installer.md).

### CI-blocker fix that opens the phase

The previous push left `shell-build.yml` red on all three legs (Windows / Linux / macOS). Two root causes, both fixed in this phase as collateral: (1) `desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` references icons under `icons/` (32x32.png, 128x128.png, 128x128@2x.png, icon.icns, icon.ico) but the icons directory was a Phase 1 placeholder (`1.P2.E`) and tauri-build refused to compile (`icons/icon.ico not found ...` on Windows; `failed to open icon ... /icons/32x32.png` on Linux). (2) `desktop/src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs` calls `app.path().resolve(...)` to find the bundled sidecar, but does not import `tauri::Manager` -- the v2.11 toolchain on `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` surfaces this as `error[E0599]: no method named path found for reference &AppHandle`. Phase 9 lands a reproducible icon generator at [scripts/desktop/generate-icons.py](../scripts/desktop/generate-icons.py) that downsizes the user-supplied [assets/nexus_primary.png](../assets/nexus_primary.png) brand mark into every PNG / ICO / ICNS / Windows Store tile size, commits the generated icon set under [desktop/src-tauri/icons/](../desktop/src-tauri/icons/), and adds the missing `Manager` import to `sidecar.rs`. Resolves known gap `1.P2.E`.

### What changed

**9.1 Architecture decision -- NSIS outer + PyQt wizard inner.** New [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/installer-architecture.md](v1/v1.0/installer-architecture.md) is the canonical decision doc. Two layers: an outer NSIS-compiled `.exe` (~200 KB) that handles UAC elevation, payload extraction to `%TEMP%\Nexus-Setup\`, manifest verification, wizard launch, and the standard Windows shell registrations (HKLM Uninstall entry, Start Menu shortcut, optional Desktop shortcut, `.nexus-workflow.json` association, `nexus://` URL handler); and the existing cross-platform PyQt5 wizard at [scripts/installer/pyqt/](../scripts/installer/pyqt/) (renamed from gemma_installer in Phase 2.5) doing every per-OS provisioning step. The wizard is PyInstaller-frozen into a single `nexus-installer.exe` shipped inside the payload tree. Decision matrix covers NSIS vs WiX/MSI/Inno (payload-size and scripting flexibility wins for NSIS); pre-bundled CUDA 12.1 runtime libraries (~1.5 GB compressed) vs full CUDA toolkit installer (runtime is all the app needs); pre-bundled wheels + `pip install --no-index` vs live PyPI (offline-first; deterministic); bundled Node 22 portable vs system Node (avoid major-version conflicts); bundled Ollama installer + `OllamaSetup.exe /S` vs manual install; network-download models via the registry's resumable downloader vs bundle models in the .exe (12-70 GB models would balloon the installer past the shareable size); frozen DevAI-Hub baseline tarball vs live `git clone` at install time. New [scripts/installer/build/windows-pipeline.md](../scripts/installer/build/windows-pipeline.md) sketches the Windows build pipeline (pin versions, hydrate `build/payload/`, compute SHA-256 manifest, PyInstaller-freeze wizard, `makensis` outer, sign, upload artifact); the 5.5-6.5 GB payload budget is documented per-component. New [.github/workflows/installer-build.yml](../.github/workflows/installer-build.yml) is the Windows installer-build CI job, currently gated behind `workflow_dispatch` until the payload-fetch script lands.

**9.2 CUDA 12.1 runtime detection + provisioner.** New [scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/cuda_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/cuda_provisioner.py) -- `detect_driver_version()` probes `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader` (falls back to `C:\Windows\System32\nvidia-smi.exe` on Windows when PATH misses); `is_cuda_12_1_supported(driver_major)` gates at `>= 530`; `decide_install_mode(driver_major, has_payload)` returns one of `"gpu"` / `"cpu-fallback"` / `"missing-payload"` ; `cpu_fallback_dialog_text()` is the user-facing copy when the host has no GPU. `CudaProvisioner(payload_dir).install(log)` copies `payload/cuda-12.1-runtime/*` into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Nexus\runtime\cuda\` (or the platform equivalent), replacing any prior target. The Python `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` / `PATH` hint helper is exposed for the caller to log.

**9.3 Python venv with offline diffusion-stack wheels.** New [scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/diffusion_venv_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/diffusion_venv_provisioner.py) -- `REQUIRED_WHEEL_PREFIXES` is the 12-entry distribution list (torch+cu121, torchvision, torchaudio, diffusers, transformers, accelerate, safetensors, xformers, Pillow, imageio, controlnet_aux, opencv_python_headless); `find_missing_wheels()` matches each prefix with a trailing hyphen to avoid `torch` shadowing `torchvision`. `DiffusionVenvProvisioner(payload_dir).preflight()` short-circuits on a missing wheel or requirements.txt before the slow path; `.create_venv()` runs `python -m venv ...` against the bundled embeddable Python; `.install_wheels()` runs `pip install --no-index --find-links wheels -r requirements.txt --disable-pip-version-check` against the new venv -- fully offline. `cuda_smoke_test_command(venv_path)` returns the argv that prints `True` when `torch.cuda.is_available()` (the Phase 9.3 acceptance criterion).

**9.4 Node 22 + Ollama provisioner.** New [scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/node_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/node_provisioner.py) -- `runtime_root()` resolves the per-user runtime path; `NodeProvisioner(payload_dir).install(log)` copies `payload/node/` into the runtime tree (replacing any prior install); `.verify()` runs `node --version` against the bundled executable; `add_to_user_path_windows(directory, log)` non-destructively prepends a directory to the user's `HKCU\Environment\Path` (reads-then-writes via `winreg`, uses `REG_EXPAND_SZ`, no-op on non-Windows hosts); `ollama_service_running_windows()` returns `True` when `sc query Ollama` reports `STATE: RUNNING`; `run_bundled_ollama_setup(payload_dir, log)` runs the bundled `OllamaSetup.exe /S` silently with a graceful non-Windows short-circuit.

**9.5 Recommended-models picker page.** New [scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/pages/recommended_models.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/pages/recommended_models.py) -- three preset bundles: Light (8 GB VRAM, ~12 GB on disk: Gemma 4 E2B + SDXL Turbo + LTX-Video), Recommended (12 GB+, ~25 GB: Gemma 4 E4B + Llama 3.1 8B + SDXL Turbo + LTX-Video + SVD), Full (24 GB+, ~70 GB: Gemma 4 26B MoE + Llama 3.1 8B + Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B + SDXL 1.0 + Flux Schnell + LTX-Video + SVD + CogVideoX 2B). Each preset is a card with a radio toggle and per-model checkboxes so the user can deselect individual entries; `pick_default_preset(vram_gb)` picks the largest fitting preset; an Advanced tab placeholder hosts the full registry catalog (Phase 10 sync populates this). Footer shows total GB + estimated minutes via `estimate_download_minutes(total_gb, mbps=200)`. A Skip checkbox lets the user finish the install and run `nexus models install ...` later. `ModelSelection` dataclass carries `preset | selected_models | skipped` for the InstallEngine. The page is not yet inserted into `window.py`'s step controller (known gap `9.P2.DDD`).

**9.6 Frozen DevAI-Hub baseline manifest + provisioner.** New [scripts/installer/devai-hub-baseline.json](../scripts/installer/devai-hub-baseline.json) records the pinned tag + SHA + content hash + install target + namespace. New [scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/devai_hub_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/src/nexus_installer/engine/devai_hub_provisioner.py) -- `DevAIBaselineManifest.from_json()` parses the manifest; `sha256_file()` returns the `sha256:<hex>` content hash; `DevAIHubProvisioner(payload_dir, manifest_path).install(log)` verifies the tarball SHA against the manifest (skips when the manifest's hash is the placeholder zero string), then extracts via a path-traversal-hardened `_safe_extract()` that resolves every member path against the target root and rejects entries that escape (CVE-2007-4559 mitigation), passing `filter="data"` so the Python 3.12+ extractor uses the standard-library hardened filter too. Pinned SHAs are placeholder zeros until DevAI-Hub@v1.0.0-baseline is cut (known gap `9.P1.AAA`).

**9.7 NSIS outer installer template.** New [scripts/installer/build/nsis/nexus-setup.nsi](../scripts/installer/build/nsis/nexus-setup.nsi) -- MUI2 wizard pages, `RequestExecutionLevel admin`, payload `File /r` extraction, manifest verification step (`nexus-installer.exe --verify-only`), wizard launch with `--install-dir`, HKLM Uninstall registry entry with full metadata (DisplayName / DisplayVersion / Publisher / URLInfoAbout / InstallLocation / UninstallString / EstimatedSize / NoModify / NoRepair), Start Menu shortcut, optional Desktop shortcut, `.nexus-workflow.json` -> `Nexus.Workflow` ProgID with `shell\open\command`, `nexus://` URL handler under `HKCR\nexus\shell\open\command`, and an uninstaller that prompts whether to preserve `~\.nexus\` (models + skills + settings; default keep) before removing the program runtime and every registry entry. End-to-end `makensis` build is not yet exercised in CI (known gap `9.P1.CCC`).

**9.8 macOS + Linux scope.** New [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/installer-macos-and-linux.md](v1/v1.0/installer-macos-and-linux.md) scopes the cross-platform installers: macOS DMG (Universal binary; Apple Developer ID + notarization; MPS path on Apple Silicon; CPU fallback on Intel) for v1.0.1; Linux AppImage (statically linked to glibc 2.31+; same CUDA detection as Windows; ROCm deferred to v1.1.0+) for v1.0.2. The cross-platform PyQt wizard is reused unchanged; only the outer-shell packaging and the GPU-detection per-platform branches differ. New [.github/workflows/installer-macos.yml](../.github/workflows/installer-macos.yml) and [.github/workflows/installer-linux.yml](../.github/workflows/installer-linux.yml) are workflow_dispatch CI placeholders.

**9.9 Tests + smoke checklist.** Added 59 new installer unit tests across [test_cuda_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/tests/test_cuda_provisioner.py) (15 tests: driver-version parsing, CUDA 12.1 driver gate, decision-table, dialog copy, no-payload path, happy-path copy, replace-existing-target), [test_diffusion_venv_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/tests/test_diffusion_venv_provisioner.py) (9 tests: missing-wheels detection with prefix-collision guard, preflight pass/fail, venv-create subprocess plumbing, install-wheels failure, smoke-test command), [test_node_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/tests/test_node_provisioner.py) (12 tests: runtime root, platform-specific executable suffix, install + replace, verify failure, PATH non-Windows short-circuit, Ollama helper guards), [test_recommended_models.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/tests/test_recommended_models.py) (16 tests: preset data integrity, increasing VRAM, default-preset picker across the spectrum, download-time estimator, total-GB summation, page renders for high + low VRAM), [test_devai_hub_provisioner.py](../scripts/installer/pyqt/tests/test_devai_hub_provisioner.py) (7 tests: manifest parsing, no-tarball warning, happy-path extract + log, replace-existing target, content-hash mismatch is fatal, correct-hash succeeds, **path-traversal evil-tarball rejected before any file is written**). New [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/installer-smoke-checklist.md](v1/v1.0/installer-smoke-checklist.md) is the operator-facing manual checklist for the fresh-Windows-11-VM install gate; the v1.0.0-rc1 build is the first scheduled run.

## [2026-05-17] v1.0.0 Phase 8 -- GpuScheduler + Local Model Status dashboard widget

### Goal

Resolve four-pillars-on-one-GPU contention with a cross-module FIFO scheduler that enforces foreground-module-wins ordering and per-job VRAM gating; ship a 2 Hz GPU telemetry source that publishes `gpu.sample` events on the existing `TelemetryBus`; light up the Phase 1.6 `<LocalModelStatus>` widget against the real telemetry stream with hover tooltip + click-to-open queue modal + idle state + floating placement on every module page; and extend the existing 3-tier `HardwareTier` LLM classification with a parallel four-tier `DiffusionTier` that gates Image Studio + Video Lab defaults by VRAM. The Phase 8 stability gate is "a Video Lab job, then Image Studio img2img, then Chatbot long generation queue without overlap and the dashboard reflects live GPU% / free VRAM without OOM". Plan reference: [docs/versions/v1/v1.0.0/plans/phase-08-gpu-scheduler-and-telemetry.md](v1/v1.0/plans/phase-08-gpu-scheduler-and-telemetry.md).

### What changed

**8.1 GpuScheduler.** New [core/scheduler/GpuScheduler.ts](../core/scheduler/GpuScheduler.ts) is a shared-core service. Each pillar `enqueue()`s a `GpuJob` (moduleId in `{coding, chat, image, video}`, `jobType`, `estimatedVramGB`, `priority`, `modelId`, `run(signal)`); the scheduler resolves free VRAM via an injected `vramProvider`, rejects requests above the ceiling with `InsufficientVramError`, returns a `JobHandle` (id + completion promise + cancel + state), and pumps the queue one job at a time (single-GPU ceiling). `setForegroundModule(id)` reorders pending entries so jobs whose `moduleId === id` move to the head of the queue while preserving relative FIFO order among themselves and the bumped-down background jobs. `cancel()` aborts a pending entry immediately (`state === "cancelled"` + queue drop + `JobCancelledError` rejection); on a running job it fires the AbortSignal and the run callback's own abort handling closes the loop. Every state transition publishes a `job.queued` / `job.started` / `job.completed` / `job.failed` event on the `TelemetryBus` with `source: "gpu-scheduler"` and a payload carrying the originating module + job metadata. `job.cancelled` is published with `kind: "job.failed"` and `payload.schedulerEvent: "job.cancelled"` until the `TelemetryEventKind` union is widened (known-gap `8.P2.YY`). `snapshot()` returns the active + queued lists for the telemetry widget. The Coding module integration note (only the streaming-LLM-token-generation call enqueues a job; tool calls are CPU-bound and bypass the scheduler) is captured in the file header docblock so future call-site wiring stays consistent.

**8.2 GpuTelemetrySource.** New [core/telemetry/GpuTelemetrySource.ts](../core/telemetry/GpuTelemetrySource.ts) polls the host GPU at 2 Hz (every 500 ms, overridable) via an injected `GpuQueryFn` and publishes `gpu.sample` events on the `TelemetryBus`. Parsing is pulled out as three pure functions: `parseNvidiaSmiCsv(text)` handles the `utilization.gpu, memory.total, memory.free, name` CSV line (header tolerated, CRLF tolerated, clamps utilization to 0..100); `parseAppleSystemProfiler(text, fallbackRamGB)` parses `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json` for sppci_model + spdisplays_vram (handles "16 GB" and "8192 MB" suffixes); `buildCpuFallbackSample(name, totalRamGB, freeRamGB)` emits the CPU-only fallback with `device: "cpu"`. The runtime composes a `GpuQueryResult` with `device | deviceName | utilizationPct | totalVramGB | freeVramGB`; the source then decorates with an active-job snapshot from a caller-supplied `activeJobProvider()` (typically the scheduler's snapshot) and stamps `capturedAt`. `start()` is idempotent; `stop()` is safe to call before start. CPU degrade is automatic on query reject or null result. The platform-specific `nvidia-smi -lms 500` long-lived child-process driver is deferred (known-gap `8.P1.UU`); the pure parsers + plug-in `GpuQueryFn` keep the unit tests hermetic.

**8.3 Local Model Status widget light-up.** Extended [desktop/src/components/LocalModelStatus.types.ts](../desktop/src/components/LocalModelStatus.types.ts) with optional `vramTotalGB`, `vramAllocatedGB`, `queuedJobs[]`, and `idle` fields (back-compat additive). Rewrote [desktop/src/components/LocalModelStatus.tsx](../desktop/src/components/LocalModelStatus.tsx) so the widget surface is a `<button>` (clickable, focusable, ARIA-labelled); the `title` attribute carries a multi-line tooltip with device / total VRAM / allocated VRAM / free VRAM / queued-jobs breakdown; the idle state renders "Idle" with a muted accent; clicking opens an in-place modal (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`) that lists every queued job by module / type / VRAM estimate or shows an empty state. New [desktop/src/components/LocalModelStatusDock.tsx](../desktop/src/components/LocalModelStatusDock.tsx) wraps the widget in a fixed bottom-right dock at width 280 px so the four module pages share a consistent placement; [desktop/src/App.tsx](../desktop/src/App.tsx) mounts the dock on every non-dashboard route via a `useLocation()` gate (Dashboard's inline placement is unchanged). New [desktop/src/lib/telemetryStream.ts](../desktop/src/lib/telemetryStream.ts) is the bridge between the sidecar-side `GpuTelemetrySource` (raw `gpu.sample` events) and the widget's `LocalModelTelemetry` contract: a `createTelemetryStream({ source, scheduler, resolver })` factory wires a generic subscription callback into the widget shape, resolves model param-size via a `ModelMetadataResolver` (default heuristic strips `B`-suffix tokens; custom resolvers can hit `ModelRegistry`), and reference-counts upstream subscriptions so it detaches when the last consumer leaves.

**8.4 DiffusionTier.** New [core/config/DiffusionTier.ts](../core/config/DiffusionTier.ts) classifies VRAM (in GB, not MB) into four tiers (`diffusion-low` 4-8 GB / `diffusion-mid` 8-12 GB / `diffusion-high` 12-20 GB / `diffusion-pro` 20+ GB) and ships per-tier `image` defaults (width / height / steps / sampler / model / allowControlNet / allowControlNetStacking / allowLoRA) plus `video` defaults (model / clipSeconds / fps / dimensions / enabled). Low tier ships SD 1.5 at 512x512 with video disabled; mid ships SDXL Turbo at 1024x1024 with single ControlNet and LTX-Video 4 s @ 480p; high adds ControlNet stacking and bumps LTX to 8 s @ 720p; pro ships Flux + CogVideoX 5B with the `parallelJobs` flag set. `classifyDiffusionTier(gb)` is the auto-detector; `resolveDiffusionTier(gb, override)` fuses an auto-detected tier with an optional user override and reports whether the override was applied. Auto-detection from `GpuTelemetrySource` + Settings UI surface + Image Studio / Video Lab default-wiring are deferred (known-gaps `8.P2.WW` and `8.P2.XX`).

**8.5 Testing.** Added 66 new core tests (16 `GpuScheduler` unit tests covering FIFO + foreground-bump + VRAM gating + cancel-while-queued + cancel-while-running + failure surfaces + snapshot + custom id generator + caller-supplied job id + double-cancel + foreground-module getter + integration with three contending modules; 21 `GpuTelemetrySource` unit tests covering nvidia-smi CSV parsing happy path + header tolerance + CRLF + clamp + malformed; Apple system_profiler parsing with explicit VRAM + MB suffix + fallback RAM hint + malformed; CPU fallback shape; the `GpuTelemetrySource` runtime's sample / decorate / clamp / reject-fallback / null-fallback / start-idempotent / stop-safe / lastSample / default-no-query paths; 26 `DiffusionTier` tests covering classification across the four tier ranges + edge cases + override fusion + invalid override fall-through + each tier's image + video defaults; 3 cross-module integration tests in [tests/integration/gpu-scheduler-multi-module.test.ts](../tests/integration/gpu-scheduler-multi-module.test.ts) driving a Coding + Image + Video sequence with no-overlap assertion + mid-flight foreground switch reorder + scheduler-driven telemetry decoration). Coverage on the new core files: `core/scheduler/GpuScheduler.ts` 98.7% lines / 90.56% branches / 100% functions; `core/telemetry/GpuTelemetrySource.ts` 98.74% lines / 86.66% branches / 100% functions; `core/config/DiffusionTier.ts` 100% lines / 100% branches / 100% functions -- aggregate 99.02% lines / 89.76% branches / 100% functions, comfortably above the 80% gate. 7 new desktop tests on the `telemetryStream` adapter; 6 new widget tests (idle, tooltip, click-to-open modal, empty-state modal, 0->80% sweep); 2 dock tests. Desktop coverage on the Phase 8 surfaces: `LocalModelStatus.tsx` 99.59% lines, `LocalModelStatusDock.tsx` 100%, `telemetryStream.ts` 100%. Pre-existing CRLF/LF snapshot failures in `tests/unit/agents/SubAgentManager.characterization.test.ts` (4 tests) are unchanged from the Phase 2 baseline (known-gap `2.P3.L`).

### Outcome

- `npm test` (full main suite): 2951 / 2960 pass, 5 skipped, 4 failed -- the 4 failures are all in `SubAgentManager.characterization.test.ts`, pre-existing CRLF/LF snapshot mismatches tracked as known-gap `2.P3.L`; no new failures from Phase 8.
- `npm test --workspace @nexus/desktop`: 351 / 351 pass.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` (main + desktop): clean.
